headline: TSE calls it for Lula, 51.76% to 48.24%, first first-round runner-up ever to win a runoff
dek: TSE called Brazil's presidential runoff for incumbent Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva over Senator Flavio Bolsonaro at about 21:13 Brasilia time (00:13 GMT, 04:13 ), ending the HOLD status of totw-20261026-0400-02 (count at 51.94%). Timed TSE snapshot 21:24 Brasilia: 99.86% of sections counted…
sources: Brazil Superior Electoral Court (TSE) call and official results dashboard, via Reuters; TSE snapshot figures via JBizNews dashboard read
fault_line: Stolen-by-extension vs counted-fair: was Zanin's two-hour extension (granted on Lula's campaign request, Zanin having been Lula's lawyer before joining the court in 2023) emergency access for stranded voters, or a thumb

sections.what_happened: TSE called Brazil's presidential runoff for incumbent Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva over Senator Flavio Bolsonaro at about 21:13 Brasilia time (00:13 GMT, 04:13 ), ending the HOLD status of totw-20261026-0400-02 (count at 51.94%). Timed TSE snapshot 21:24 Brasilia: 99.86% of sections counted (498,538 of 499,248), Lula 64,137,770 votes = 51.76% of valid votes, Bolsonaro 59,769,627 = 48.24%, margin 4,368,143 valid votes; 123,907,397 valid, 1,428,694 blank, 2,719,197 invalid of 128,055,288 ballots processed. Lula secures a fourth non-consecutive term and becomes the first candidate to trail after a first round (Oct 4: Bolsonaro 47%, Lula 45%) and win the runoff since Brazil adopted the system in 1989. He turns 81 on Tuesday Oct 27 and is to be sworn in Jan 5, 2027 (AJ). SCMP's near-final read matches: 51.76% to 48.24% at 99.83% counted. Earlier snapshots differ only by time (AFP via Vanguard: 51.75% to 48.25%; an earlier SSBCrack read: 51.52% to 48.48%) -- figures are a timed snapshot, not a 100% final tally.
sections.what_verified: TSE itself called the race; the call is carried by Reuters and Al Jazeera, and the 51.76/48.24 split is independently shown by the TSE dashboard read and SCMP. The result is confirmed as a called result; the exact final percentages await the 100% tally.
sections.what_disputed: No Flavio Bolsonaro concession statement was retrieved by the 05:05 final check; an ANI early-count carry notes he did not immediately concede, but that carry predates the call and is not a post-call statement. SCMP warns the outcome could still be contested over Justice Zanin's two-hour extension: stations that had already closed their machines could not reopen, so some voters were sent home at 17:00 while others voted until 19:00; any annulment request would go to the TSE, chaired by Kassio Nunes Marques, Jair Bolsonaro's first Supreme Court appointee. Partisan fraud claims circulating on GETTR/social (extension = rigging) are ALLEGATION, not evidence, and are not corroboration of any irregularity.
sections.why_matters: The comeback no runoff had ever produced: the first-round loser beats the Bolsonaro name -- and the fight now moves from the count to the two-hour extension.
sections.context: Background: IN-WINDOW ELEVATION -- Brazil runoff RESULT: TSE calls it for Lula, 51.76% to 48.24%, first first-round runner-up ever to win a runoff

totw_analysis: Our read: The comeback no runoff had ever produced: the first-round loser beats the Bolsonaro name -- and the fight now moves from the count to the two-hour extension. The fault line our audience is arguing over: Stolen-by-extension vs counted-fair: was Zanin's two-hour extension (granted on Lula's campaign request, Zanin having been Lula's lawyer before joining the court in 2023) emergency access for stranded voters, or a thumb on the scale for the incumbent?
